ai.description: This small skink reaches 45 mm in snout-vent length. It is brown above with a dark lateral stripe and yellowish belly. It is distinguished by a single pair of supranasals and smooth midbody scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: Distinguish *Ristella travancorica* from other Indian Ristella species by the presence of a distinct, enlarged, and shield-like supranasal scale that touches the nostril.
ai.habitat: The Travancore Ristella inhabits leaf litter within moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Travancore Ristella is a diurnal lizard that actively hunts for small insects and invertebrates among leaf litter on the forest floor.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ristella travancorica* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, spanning from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Travancore Ristella is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting moist forests at elevations between 500 and 1,500 meters.
